To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have generated a set of monoclonal antibodies that recognize the individual members of two families of cell cycle regulatory proteins (CKIs), and have characterized these reagents as tools for analyses of the cellular and tissue distribution of these proteins, their subcellular localization and interacting partners.

we have isolated, characterized, and validated a panel of MAbs to the INK4 and Cip/Kip families of CKIs that are proving invaluable in analyses of these cell cycle regulatory proteins in cells and tissues.
a series of 10 monoclonal antibodies that specifically recognize p15, p16, p18, p19, or p21 have been generated and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular mechanisms of tumor suppression and cancer progression, in particular, the role played by the CKIs.
the isolation, characterization and application of MAbs that specifically recognize p15, p16, p18, p19, and p21.
the development and characterization of monoclonal antibodies that recognize the individual members of two families of cell cycle regulators, the Cip/Kips and INK4s.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these antibodies are invaluable molecular probes to study the CKIs in cells or tissue samples.
the MAbs developed and described here are proving to be valuable tools in the analysis of the CKIs.

the panel of antibodies we describe in this study are proving to be valuable tools to study CKIs, a set of reagents that will help elucidate their physiological roles, as well as the molecular mechanisms of their loss or inactivation in human malignancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these MAbs are proving invaluable molecular probes for analysis of protein abundance, localization, interacting proteins, and ultimately function of CKIs in cells, tissues and tumors.
we have developed a panel of monoclonal antibodies for the INK4 and Cip/Kip CKIs that will help to further elucidate the biological functions of the individual CKIs.

we have developed a panel of MAbs to the INK4 and Cip/Kip CKIs that should prove useful for the study of these proteins in normal and neoplastic tissues, including their use in the development of diagnostic tests for the assessment of tumor progression and prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a panel of MAbs directed against the same protein can provide a wealth of information that would not be available with a single MAb, and that this approach is particularly useful when studying the CKIs.
MAbs are powerful reagents to study proteins in cells and tissues.
a panel of monoclonal antibodies to the individual members of a protein family is a powerful tool to study the individual members of such a family, as well as the family as a whole.
